# Online Etymology Dictionary

> > Comprehensive dictionary tracing English word origins through Old English, Latin, Proto-Germanic, Greek, and other historical language roots.

The Online Etymology Dictionary provides detailed etymological information for English words, documenting their evolution through Old English, Middle English, Latin, Proto-Germanic, Old French, Old Norse, and other ancestral languages. Founded by etymologist Douglas Harper, the site serves as a scholarly resource for understanding how words have changed in form and meaning over centuries.

## Key Topics

- Old English
- Proto-Indo-European (PIE)
- Latin roots
- Proto-Germanic
- Middle English
- Old French
- Germanic languages
- Old Norse
- Greek origins
- Semantic shift
- Historical linguistics
- Word formation
- Language evolution
- Etymology research

## Common Words & Everyday Language

- [Misspell - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/misspell): Etymology of 'misspell' from Proto-Germanic through Old English origins
- [Sneaky - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/sneaky): 1833 adjective from sneak + -y suffix, Proto-Germanic roots
- [Marketing - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/marketing): Business term evolution from market transactions to Listerine campaigns
- [Childbirth - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/childbirth): Mid-15c compound from child + birth, Proto-Germanic origins
- [Flashlight - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/flashlight): American English term from flash + light, British 'torch' equivalent

## Words with Semantic Shifts

- [Blindfold - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/blindfold): Word origin of 'blindfold' showing Middle English semantic shift
- [Rarity - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/rarity): French/Latin origin showing semantic evolution from 'thinness' to 'fewness'
- [Resurrect - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/resurrect): 1772 back-formation from resurrection via Church Latin origins
- [Redundance - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/redundance): Latin redundantia meaning 'superfluity, overflowing' word history

## Brand Names & Modern Coinages

- [Muzak - Etymology, Origin & Meaning of the Name](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Muzak): 1935 brand name coined by Gen. George Squier blending music + Kodak
- [Wingding - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/wingding): Etymology of 'wingding' from hobo slang to Microsoft Wingdings font

## Technical & Specialized Terms

- [Phallocentric - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/phallocentric): 1927 psychoanalysis term from Greek phallus + -centric roots
- [Soteriological - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/soteriological): 1843 theological term from Greek for Christian salvation doctrine
- [Indigency - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/indigency): Latin-origin word meaning 'need, want' through Old French
- [Irrelevance - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/irrelevance): 1735 formation from irrelevant + -ance suffix, Latin roots

## Alphabet & Letters

- [Y - Etymology, Origin & Meaning of the Name](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Y): Letter Y history from Greek through Middle English scribal practices
- [V - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/V): Letter V as Roman numeral and consonant evolution in Middle English

## Historical & Archaic Terms

- [Childe - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/childe): Old English archaic title meaning 'youth of gentle birth'
- [Caboose - Etymology, Origin & Meaning](https://www.etymonline.com/word/caboose): Dutch maritime term evolving to railroad car via Low German roots
